(7) A magistrate may issue a warrant to enter a non-mine place only on written application under oath showing necessity.
(7A) An inspector may impose a prohibition on further site functioning by blocking, barring, or barricading it, where death, serious injury/illness, or a health-threatening occurrence has occurred.
(8) "Mine" for this section excludes any home or residential quarters situated at the mine.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Inspector may be accompanied
body: When performing any function under this Act, an inspector may be accompanied by an interpreter or any other person reasonably required to assist the inspector.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Duty to assist inspector and answer questions
body:
(1) When an inspector enters a mine or place, the employer and each employee there must provide any facility the inspector reasonably requires.
(2) Persons questioned by an inspector must answer to the best of their ability, but are not required to answer self-incriminating questions.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Duty to produce documents required by inspector
body: Any person who holds or should hold a permit, licence, permission, certificate, authorisation, or other document issued under this Act or the Mineral and Petroleum Resources Development Act must produce it at the request of the Chief Inspector of Mines or any inspector.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Inspectors' power to order compliance
body:
(1) If an inspector believes an employer has failed to comply with this Act, the inspector may instruct that employer in writing to take steps the inspector considers necessary and specifies.
(2) The instruction must specify a compliance period, which an inspector may extend at any time by written notice.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Inspector's powers to recommend fine
body:
(1) An inspector may recommend in writing to the Principal Inspector of Mines that a fine be imposed on a non-compliant employer.
(3) The inspector must serve a copy of the recommendation on the employer, the health and safety committee (or representative), and the representative trade union (or all registered trade unions with members at the mine).
(4) The employer may make written representations within 30 days.
(5) A representation made under this section may not be used against the employer in criminal or civil proceedings on the same facts.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Principal Inspector of Mines may impose fines
body:
(1) The Principal Inspector of Mines, after considering the recommendation and any representations, may disregard the recommendation, impose a fine up to the maximum in Table 2 of Schedule 8, or refer the matter to the prosecuting authority.
(2) The Principal Inspector must notify the employer, committee, representative, and trade union of the decision.
(3) The employer must pay any fine within 30 days.
(4) If unpaid, the Chief Inspector of Mines may apply to the Labour Court for the fine to be made an order of that court.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Instructions to be posted at mine
body: The employer of a mine must promptly supply a copy of any inspector's instruction to the relevant health and safety representative and committee, and promptly publicise it by prominently displaying copies to affected employees and communicating its contents to them orally.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Right to appeal inspectors' decisions
body:
(1) Any person adversely affected by an inspector's decision (except a decision under section 55B) may appeal to the Chief Inspector of Mines.
(2) An appeal must be lodged within 30 days (or a further prescribed period) and set out the grounds.
(3) The Chief Inspector must, as soon as practicable, confirm, set aside, vary, or substitute the decision.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Right to appeal Chief Inspector of Mines' decision
body:
(1) Any person adversely affected by a decision of the Chief Inspector of Mines may appeal to the Labour Court.
(2) The appeal must be lodged with the Labour Court registrar within 60 days of the decision.
(3) The Labour Court must consider the appeal and confirm, set aside, or vary the decision.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Appeal does not suspend decision
body:
(1) An appeal against a decision under sections 57 or 58 does not suspend the decision.
(2) However, an appeal against a decision to impose a fine suspends the obligation to pay pending the outcome, and the Labour Court may suspend the operation of a decision on reasonable grounds.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Initiating investigations
body:
(1) The Chief Inspector of Mines must instruct an inspector to investigate any accident or occurrence resulting in death.
(2) An inspector may at any time investigate serious injury or illness, health/safety-related occurrences/practices/conditions, or actual/suspected contraventions.
(3) An inspector must investigate if there is cause for concern and instructed to do so, or requested by a registered trade union, health and safety representative/committee, or (if none) an employee.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Chief Inspector of Mines may designate assistant in investigation
body: At any time before or during an investigation, the Chief Inspector of Mines may designate one or more persons to assist the inspector holding the investigation.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Duty to answer questions during investigation
body: Persons questioned during an investigation must answer every question to the best of their ability, but no person is required to answer any question if the answer may be self-incriminating.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Enhancing effectiveness of investigation
body:
(1) The National Prosecuting Authority, after receiving representations from the Chief Inspector of Mines, may issue a certificate that no prosecution may be instituted for contraventions related to the investigated event; if issued, no fine or disciplinary action related to that event may thereafter be imposed.
(2) The Chief Inspector must communicate this protection in writing to all persons questioned.
(3) Protected persons must answer every question to the best of their ability and may not refuse on self-incrimination grounds.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Reports on investigations
body:
(1) After an investigation, an inspector must prepare a written report of findings, recommendations, and remedial steps.
(2) The inspector must submit a copy to the Chief Inspector of Mines, supply a copy to the employer and the requesting party, and may instruct the employer to display the report for employees to read.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Initiating inquiries
body:
(1) Unless section 63 has been invoked, the Chief Inspector must direct an inspector to conduct an inquiry into any death.
(2) The Chief Inspector may direct an inquiry into serious injury/illness, health/safety occurrences, or actual/suspected contraventions.
(3) If there is cause for concern and section 63 hasn't been invoked, the Chief Inspector may direct an inquiry if requested by a registered trade union, health and safety representative/committee, or (if none) an employee.
(4) This section doesn't limit other laws regulating inquests or inquiries into a death.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Investigation may be converted into inquiry
body:
(1) At any time during an investigation, the Chief Inspector of Mines may convert it into an inquiry.
(2) The provisions on attendance and examination of witnesses at inquiries apply equally to a converted investigation.
(3) A person instructed or summoned at a converted inquiry isn't entitled to refuse to give evidence merely because a statement was previously given during the investigation.
(4) This doesn't preclude holding an inquiry after an investigation is completed.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Chief Inspector of Mines may designate assistant in inquiry
body: At any time before or during an inquiry, the Chief Inspector of Mines may designate one or more persons to assist in or preside at the inquiry.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Inquiry to be public
body:
(1) An inquiry must be held in public.
(2) The presiding person may exclude the public or specific persons when proper conduct of the inquiry requires it.
(3) The presiding person may order that employees and the public have access to the premises where the inquiry is held.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Right to participate in inquiry
body: Persons who may participate in an inquiry, personally or through a representative, putting questions to witnesses and inspecting documents, are: any person with a material interest in the inquiry, a representative of any registered trade union with members at the mine, and any health and safety representative responsible for the relevant working place.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Powers of person presiding at inquiry
body: The person presiding at an inquiry may instruct or summon any person to appear at a specified time and place, question any person under oath, and instruct any person to produce documents or items or perform other necessary acts for the inquiry.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Duty of persons summoned or instructed
body:
(1) Every person giving evidence at an inquiry must answer any relevant question.
(2) Ordinary court witness privilege applies equally at an inquiry.
(3) The presiding person may direct that evidence given may not be used in criminal or disciplinary proceedings except for perjury.
(4) When such a directive is issued, the person may not refuse to answer on self-incrimination grounds.
(5) A person instructed under section 70(c) must comply unless they have sufficient cause not to.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Inquiry records and reports
body:
(1) The presiding person must record the evidence given, prepare a written report of findings/recommendations/remedial steps, submit a copy with the record to the Chief Inspector of Mines, supply copies to the employer and requesting parties, and supply copies on request to anyone with a material interest.
(2) An inspector may instruct the employer to display the report for employees to read.
(3) The Chief Inspector may submit a copy to the appropriate Attorney-General.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Chief Inspector of Mines may order further inquiry
body: Upon considering the evidence and report from an inquiry, the Chief Inspector of Mines may require that the matter be inquired into further.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Inquiry and inquest may be conducted jointly
body:
(1) An inquiry into a death may be held jointly with an inquest under the Inquests Act, 1959.
(2) The judicial officer under the Inquests Act must preside, and the person instructed to hold the inquiry under this Act is deemed an assessor under the Inquests Act.
(3) The Inquests Act's provisions apply to a joint inquiry.
(4) The assessor must prepare a report and submit it with the record to the Chief Inspector of Mines.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Minister may prohibit or restrict work
body:
(1) For health or safety reasons, the Minister, by Gazette notice, may prohibit or restrict any work or exposure to a substance or environmental condition, after consulting the Council, and (unless urgent public interest requires immediate publication) after publishing a draft notice at least three months prior and inviting comment.
(2) The Minister may attach conditions to a prohibition or restriction.
(3) The Minister, after consulting the Council, may amend or withdraw such a notice at any time.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Minister may declare health hazards
body:
(1) The Minister, by Gazette notice after consulting the Council (and following the same draft-and-comment process as section 75 unless urgent), may declare an environmental condition or substance at a mine to be a health hazard.
(2) The Minister may then impose conditions on affected work, stipulate fitness standards, require risk elimination measures, require occupational hygiene measurements or medical surveillance, and provide for other necessary protective matters.
(3) The Minister may enter any mine at any time, but only for health hazard purposes.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Application of Minister's notice
body: A notice under section 75 or 76 may differentiate between mines, types of mines, parts of a mine, occupations, and types of work.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Exemption from Minister's notice
body:
(1) A notice under either section 75 or 76 may exempt a particular person or group of persons from compliance with that notice if the Minister is satisfied that any of the following conditions exists: the circumstances make the exemption desirable, the performance of the work by that person or group is temporary, or the risk to which that person or group is exposed is not significant enough to warrant the notice applying to them.
(2) The Minister, after consulting the Council, may cancel an exemption granted under subsection (1) at any time.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Exemption from all or part of this Act
body:
(1) The employer of a mine may request an exemption from the Minister, and if satisfied that the employer has consulted appropriately with the affected employees or their representatives, the Minister may exempt the employer from any or all the provisions of this Act or from a notice or instruction issued under this Act.
(3) The Minister may amend or withdraw a certificate of exemption at any time.
(4) The employer must prominently and conspicuously display any exemption granted, or deemed to have been granted, under this section to the employees to read.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Minister may apply other laws to mine
body:
(1) After consulting the Council, the Minister, by notice in the Gazette, may declare that any provision of the Occupational Health and Safety Act, 1993 (Act No. 85 of 1993), or any regulation made under that Act, or the provisions of any other Act or regulations, must apply to a mine.
(2) A declaration under subsection (1) may differentiate between mines, types of mines, parts of a mine, occupations, and types of work.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Minister to table annual report
body: Within 30 days of receiving the annual report of the Chief Inspector of Mines, the Minister must table it in Parliament.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Definitions

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Inclusion of provisions in contracts of employment
body:
A basic condition of employment constitutes a term of any contract of employment except to the extent that-
(a) any other law provides a term that is more favourable to the employee;
(b) the basic condition of employment has been replaced, varied, or excluded in accordance with the provisions of this Act; or
(c) a term of the contract of employment is more favourable to the employee than the basic condition of employment.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: This Act not affected by agreements
body: This Act or anything done under it takes precedence over any agreement, whether entered into before or after the commencement of this Act.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Interpretation of day
body: For the purposes of sections 9 to 16, "day" means a period of 24 hours measured from the time when the employee normally commences work, and "daily" has a corresponding meaning.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Compressed working week
body:
(1) An agreement in writing may require or permit an employee to work up to twelve hours in a day, inclusive of the meal intervals required in terms of section 14, without receiving overtime pay.
(2) An agreement in terms of subsection (1) may not require or permit an employee to work more than 45 ordinary hours of work in any week, more than ten hours' overtime in any week, or on more than five days in any week.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Averaging of hours of work
body:
(1) Despite sections 9(1) and (2) and 10(1)(b), the ordinary hours of work and overtime of an employee may be averaged over a period of up to four months in terms of a collective agreement.
(2) An employer may not require or permit an employee who is bound by a collective agreement in terms of subsection (1) to work more than an average of 45 ordinary hours of work in a week over the agreed period, or an average of five hours' overtime in a week over the agreed period.
(3) A collective agreement in terms of subsection (1) lapses after 12 months.
(4) Subsection (3) only applies to the first two collective agreements concluded in terms of subsection (1).

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Determination of hours of work by Minister
body:
(1) Despite this Chapter, the Minister, on grounds of health and safety, may prescribe by regulation the maximum permitted hours of work, including overtime, that any category of employee may work daily, weekly or during any other period specified, and during a continuous period without a break.
(2) A regulation in terms of subsection (1) may not prescribe maximum hours in excess of those permitted in sections 9 and 10.
(3) A regulation in terms of subsection (1) may be made only on the advice of the chief inspector appointed in terms of the Occupational Health and Safety Act, 1993, or the chief inspector appointed in terms of the Mine Health and Safety Act, 1996, and after consulting the Commission.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Application of this Chapter (leave)
body:
(1) This Chapter does not apply to an employee who works less than 24 hours a month for an employer.
(2) Unless an agreement provides otherwise, this Chapter does not apply to leave granted to an employee in excess of the employee's entitlement under this Chapter.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Pay for annual leave
body:
(1) An employer must pay an employee leave pay at least equivalent to the remuneration that the employee would have received for working for a period equal to the period of annual leave, calculated at the employee's rate of remuneration immediately before the beginning of the period of annual leave, and in accordance with section 35.
(2) An employer must pay an employee leave pay before the beginning of the period of leave, or by agreement, on the employee's usual pay day.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Application to occupational accidents or diseases
body: Sections 22 and 23 do not apply to an inability to work caused by an accident or occupational disease as defined in the Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act, 1993, or the Occupational Diseases in Mines and Works Act, 1973, except in respect of any period during which no compensation is payable in terms of those Acts.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Protection of employees before and after birth of a child
body:
(1) No employer may require or permit a pregnant employee or an employee who is nursing her child to perform work that is hazardous to her health or the health of her child.
(2) During an employee's pregnancy, and for a period of six months after the birth of her child, her employer must offer her suitable, alternative employment on terms and conditions that are no less favourable than her ordinary terms and conditions of employment, if the employee is required to perform night work or her work poses a danger to her health or safety or that of her child, and it is practicable for the employer to do so.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Application of this Chapter (particulars of employment)
body:
(1) This Chapter does not apply to an employee who works less than 24 hours a month for an employer.
(2) Sections 29(1)(n), (o) and (p), 30, 31 and 33 do not apply to an employer who employs fewer than five employees.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Written particulars of employment
body:
(1) An employer must supply an employee, when the employee commences employment, with the following particulars in writing: the full name and address of the employer; the name and occupation of the employee, or a brief description of the work; the place of work; the date employment began; the employee's ordinary hours and days of work; the employee's wage or rate and method of calculating wages; the rate of pay for overtime; any other cash payments the employee is entitled to; any payment in kind and its value; how frequently remuneration will be paid; any deductions to be made; the leave the employee is entitled to; the period of notice required to terminate employment (or the termination date if for a specified period); a description of any council or sectoral determination covering the business; any period counting towards the employee's period of employment with a previous employer; and a list of any other documents forming part of the contract, indicating where a copy may be obtained.
(2) When any listed matter changes, the written particulars must be revised and the employee supplied with a copy.
(3) If an employee cannot understand the written particulars, the employer must have them explained in a language and manner the employee understands.
(4) Written particulars must be kept for three years after termination of employment.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Informing employees of their rights
body: An employer must display at the workplace where it can be read by employees a statement in the prescribed form of the employee's rights under this Act in the official languages spoken in the workplace.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Keeping of records
body:
(1) Every employer must keep a record containing at least the employee's name and occupation, time worked, remuneration paid, date of birth of any employee under 18, and any other prescribed information.
(2) The record must be kept for three years from the date of the last entry.
(3) No person may make a false entry in the record.
(4) An employer who keeps a record in terms of this section is not required to keep any other record of time worked and remuneration paid required by any other employment law.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Payment of remuneration
body:
(1) An employer must pay remuneration paid in money in South African currency, daily, weekly, fortnightly or monthly, and in cash, by cheque or by direct deposit into an account designated by the employee.
(2) Cash or cheque payment must be given at the workplace or an agreed place, during working hours or within 15 minutes of them, in a sealed envelope which becomes the employee's property.
(3) An employer must pay remuneration not later than seven days after the completion of the period for which it is payable, or the termination of the contract of employment.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Information about remuneration
body:
(1) An employer must give an employee written information on each pay day covering the employer's name and address, the employee's name and occupation, the pay period, remuneration in money, any deductions and their purpose, the actual amount paid, and (where relevant) the rate of remuneration and overtime rate, hours worked, and hours worked on a Sunday or public holiday.
(2) This information must be given at the workplace or an agreed place, during working hours or within 15 minutes of them.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Deductions and other acts concerning remuneration
body:
(1) An employer may not make any deduction from remuneration unless the employee agrees in writing to a specified debt, or the deduction is required or permitted by law, collective agreement, court order or arbitration award.
(2) A deduction to reimburse loss or damage may only be made if the loss occurred in the course of employment and was the employee's fault, a fair procedure was followed, the amount doesn't exceed the actual loss, and total deductions don't exceed one-quarter of the employee's remuneration in money.
(4) An employer deducting an amount for payment to another person must pay it over within the specified time.
(5) An employer may not require repayment of remuneration (except overpayment errors) or require an employee to acknowledge receiving more than they actually received.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Application of this Chapter (termination)
body: This Chapter does not apply to an employee who works less than 24 hours in a month for an employer.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Payment instead of notice
body:
(1) Instead of giving notice, an employer may pay the employee the remuneration they would have received had they worked during the notice period.
(2) If an employee gives notice and the employer waives any part of it, the employer must pay the remuneration referred to in subsection (1), unless otherwise agreed.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Employees in accommodation provided by employers
body:
(1) If an employer terminates the contract of an employee residing in employer-provided accommodation before the date permitted by section 37, or in terms of section 38, the employer must provide accommodation for one month or until the contract could lawfully have ended, whichever is longer.
(2) If the employee elects to remain in the accommodation, the section 38 remuneration is reduced by the agreed value of that accommodation for the period remained.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Payments on termination
body: On termination of employment, an employer must pay an employee for any unused paid time off owed under sections 10(3) or 16(3), remuneration for any unused annual leave due under section 20(2), and, if employed longer than four months, a proportional amount for any incomplete annual leave cycle.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Employment of children of 15 years or older
body:
(1) Subject to section 43(2), the Minister may, on the advice of the Commission, make regulations to prohibit or place conditions on the employment of children who are at least 15 years of age and no longer subject to compulsory schooling.
(2) A person who employs a child in contravention of subsection (1) commits an offence.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Medical examinations
body: The Minister may, after consulting the Commission, make regulations relating to the conduct of medical examinations of children in employment.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Prohibitions
body: It is an offence to assist an employer to employ a child in contravention of this Act, or to discriminate against a person who refuses to permit a child to be employed in contravention of this Act.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Evidence of age
body: In any proceedings in terms of this Act, if the age of an employee is a relevant factor for which insufficient evidence is available, it is for the party who alleges that the employment complied with this Chapter to prove that it was reasonable for that party to believe, after investigation, that the person was not below the permitted age.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Variation by agreement
body:
(1) A collective agreement concluded in a bargaining council may alter, replace or exclude a basic condition of employment if consistent with this Act's purpose and it does not reduce protections under sections 7, 9, or a section 13 regulation; reduce night-work protections under section 17(3)-(4); reduce annual leave under section 20 to less than two weeks; reduce maternity leave under section 25; reduce sick leave under sections 22-24; or conflict with Chapter Six.
(2) Any other collective agreement may replace or exclude a basic condition to the extent permitted by this Act or a sectoral determination.
(3) An employer and employee may similarly agree to replace or exclude a basic condition to the extent permitted.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Variation by Minister
body:
(1) The Minister may, if consistent with this Act's purpose, make a determination to replace or exclude a basic condition of employment for a category of employees or employers, or for a specific employer or employee on application.
(2) A determination may not be made in respect of sections 7, 17(3)-(4), 25, 43(2), 44 or 48, or a section 13 regulation, and may only vary section 43(1) to allow children's employment in advertising, sports, artistic or cultural activities.
(3) A determination must be made on the advice of the Commission and issued by Gazette notice.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Sectoral determination
body:
(1) The Minister may make a sectoral determination establishing basic conditions of employment for employees in a sector and area.
(2) A sectoral determination must be made in accordance with this Chapter and by notice in the Gazette.
(3) If any sectoral determination, at the date the National Minimum Wage Act, 2018 was promulgated, prescribes wages higher than the national minimum wage, those wages and associated benefits must be increased proportionally to any adjustment of the national minimum wage.
(4) Notwithstanding any sectoral determination, an employer must pay a learner an allowance as prescribed in Schedule 2 of the National Minimum Wage Act, 2018, as adjusted from time to time.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Investigation
body:
(1) Before making a sectoral determination, the Minister must direct the National Minimum Wage Commission to investigate conditions of employment in the sector and area concerned.
(2) The Commission must determine terms of reference for the investigation, including the sector/area, the categories of employees, and the matters to be investigated.
(3) The Commission must publish a notice in the Gazette setting out the terms of reference and inviting public comment.
(4) If an employer or employee organisation requests an investigation, the Minister must direct the Commission to conduct one, or ask it to advise whether the investigation ought to be conducted.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Conduct of investigation
body:
(1) The Commission may question any relevant person, or require in writing that an employer, employee or other person furnish relevant information, documents or objects within a reasonable specified period.
(2) A person may not refuse to answer a relevant question they are legally obliged to answer.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Preparation of report
body:
(1) On completion of an investigation, and after considering public representations, the Commission must prepare a report.
(2) A copy must be submitted to the Director-General for information and to the Minister for consideration.
(3) The Commission must consider factors including the ability of employers to operate successfully, the impact on small/medium/micro-enterprises, cost of living, poverty alleviation, wage differentials, and likely impact on employment, health, safety and welfare.
(4) The Commission must prepare a report for the Minister with recommendations.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Making of sectoral determination
body:
(1) After considering the Commission's report, the Minister may make a sectoral determination for one or more sectors and areas.
(4) A sectoral determination may set minimum terms and remuneration rates or increases, regulate payment manner/timing, require record-keeping, regulate task-based/piecework/subcontract work, set minimum housing/sanitation standards, regulate allowances, set trade union representativeness thresholds, and establish conditions of service for labour tenants.
(6) A determination may not be made in respect of sections 7, 43(2), 44 or 48, may only vary section 43(1) for advertising/sports/artistic/cultural child employment, and may not reduce protections under sections 17(3)-(4) and 25 or a section 13 regulation.
(8) Subject to subsection (7), the Minister may publish a sectoral determination applying to employers and employees not covered by any other sectoral determination.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Period of operation of sectoral determination
body:
(1) A sectoral determination remains binding until amended, superseded, cancelled or suspended by the Minister.
(3) The Minister may, by Gazette notice, cancel or suspend any provision, or correct/clarify its meaning.
(4) Before cancelling or suspending, the Minister must announce the intention in the Gazette and allow public comment.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Legal effect of sectoral determination
body: If a matter regulated in this Act is also regulated by a sectoral determination, the sectoral determination provision prevails.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Employer to keep a copy of sectoral determination
body: Unless the determination provides otherwise, every bound employer must keep a copy available at the workplace, make it available for employee inspection, and give a copy to any employee who requests one (free for trade union representatives or workplace forum members).

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Functions of labour inspectors
body:
(1) A labour inspector may promote, monitor and enforce compliance with an employment law by advising employees and employers of their rights and obligations, conducting inspections, investigating complaints, securing undertakings or issuing compliance orders, and performing other prescribed functions.
(2) An inspector may not act where they have or may be perceived to have a personal, financial or similar interest.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Powers of entry
body:
(1) A labour inspector may, without warrant, enter any workplace or place (not a home) where an employer carries on business or keeps records, or relevant training/employment service premises.
(2) Entry to a home or other place requires consent, or Labour Court authorisation on written application under oath.
(4) Where practical, the employer and a trade union representative must be notified of the inspector's presence and reason.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Powers to question and inspect
body:
(1) A labour inspector may require disclosure of information (under oath if necessary), inspect and question about records/documents, copy or remove them, require their production, inspect and if necessary remove articles/substances/machinery, question about work performed, and perform other prescribed functions.
(3) An inspector must produce their certificate on request, provide a receipt for anything removed, and return it within a reasonable period.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Co-operation with labour inspectors
body:
(1) Any person questioned by a labour inspector must answer all relevant questions truthfully and to the best of their ability.
(2) Every employer and employee must provide reasonably required facility and assistance for the inspector to perform their functions effectively.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Securing an undertaking
body:
(1) A labour inspector with reasonable grounds to believe an employer hasn't complied with this Act, the National Minimum Wage Act, 2018, the Unemployment Insurance Act, or the Unemployment Insurance Contributions Act must endeavour to secure a written undertaking to comply, either by meeting with the employer or serving a prescribed document.
(2) The inspector may seek agreement on amounts owed, arrange payment, receive payment on an employee's written request, and must provide a receipt for any payment received.
(3) If an employer fails to comply with a written undertaking, the Director-General may request the CCMA to make the undertaking an arbitration award.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Limitations
body: A labour inspector may not issue a compliance order for an amount owing under this Act or the National Minimum Wage Act, 2018, if the employee earns in excess of the section 6(3) earnings threshold, if proceedings for recovery have been instituted in the CCMA or a court and not withdrawn, or if the amount has been owing for longer than 36 months before a complaint was made or an undertaking was first sought or a compliance order issued.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Objections to compliance order
body:
(1) An employer may object to a compliance order in writing to the Director-General within 21 days.
(2) The Director-General may permit a late objection for good cause.
(3) After considering representations, the Director-General may confirm, modify or cancel the order, specifying a new compliance period as needed.
(4) Relevant considerations include the employer's compliance record, awareness of the provisions, and compliance steps taken.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Appeals from order of Director-General
body:
(1) An employer may appeal to the Labour Court against a Director-General order within 21 days.
(2) The order is suspended pending the appeal's final determination.
(3) The Labour Court may permit a late appeal for good cause.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Order may be made an arbitration award
body:
(1) The Director-General may apply to the CCMA for a compliance order to be made an arbitration award if the employer has not complied with it.
(2) The CCMA may issue such an award if satisfied the compliance order was served on the employer and the employer has not referred a dispute under section 69(5).

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Consolidation of proceedings
body:
(1) A dispute concerning a contravention of this Act or the National Minimum Wage Act, 2018, may be instituted jointly with unfair dismissal proceedings.
(2) The Labour Court or arbitrator hearing an unfair dismissal dispute may also determine any claim for an amount owing under this Act or the National Minimum Wage Act.
(2A) No compliance order may be issued or enforced, and no other legal proceedings instituted, in respect of a claim already determined under subsection (2).
(3) A dispute about an amount owing may be joined with a severance pay entitlement dispute under section 41(6).

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Payment of interest
body: An employer must pay interest on any amount due and payable under this Act or the National Minimum Wage Act, 2018, at the rate prescribed under the Prescribed Rate of Interest Act, 1975, to any person owed payment.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Proof of compliance
body: In proceedings concerning a contravention of this Act, the National Minimum Wage Act, 2018, or a sectoral determination, it is for the employer to prove that its records are valid and accurate, or, if records were not kept as required, to prove compliance by other means.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Jurisdiction of Labour Court
body:
(1) Subject to the Constitution and the Labour Appeal Court's jurisdiction, and except where this Act provides otherwise, the Labour Court has exclusive jurisdiction in respect of all matters under this Act.
(1A) The Labour Court has exclusive jurisdiction to grant civil relief arising from a breach of sections 33A, 43, 44, 46, 48, 90 and 92.
(2) The Labour Court may review the performance of any function under this Act on any legally permissible grounds.
(3) The Labour Court has concurrent jurisdiction with civil courts over any matter concerning a contract of employment.
(5) A court without jurisdiction over such a matter may refer it to the Labour Court at any stage.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Parental leave
body:
(1) An employee, who is a parent of a child, is entitled to at least ten consecutive days parental leave.
(2) An employee may commence parental leave on the day-
(a) that the employee's child is born; or
(b) that the adoption order is granted; or
(c) that a child is placed in the care of a prospective adoptive parent by a competent court, pending the finalisation of an adoption order in respect of that child, whichever date occurs first.
(3) An employee must notify an employer in writing, unless the employee is unable to do so, of the date on which the employee intends to commence parental leave and return to work after parental leave.
(4) Notification in terms of subsection (3) must be given at least one month before the employee's child is expected to be born, or the date referred to in subsection (2)(b) or (c), or, if not reasonably practicable, as soon as reasonably practicable.
(5) The payment of parental benefits will be determined by the Minister subject to the provisions of the Unemployment Insurance Act, 2001 (Act No. 63 of 2001).

IMPORTANT NOTE ON THIS SECTION: On 3 October 2025, the Constitutional Court (Van Wyk and Others v Minister of Employment and Labour) declared sections 25, 25A, 25B and 25C of this Act unconstitutional for discriminating between mothers, fathers, and different categories of parents. The Court suspended its order for 36 months to give Parliament time to properly rewrite these sections, but ordered an interim reading-in that applies immediately: broadly, two employed parents now share a pool of four months plus ten days of parental leave between them however they choose, and a single parent or the only employed parent in a relationship is entitled to the full four months. Section 25A is effectively removed under this interim scheme, and adoption/commissioning parental leave (sections 25B/25C) are aligned to the same shared structure, with the "under two years old" age limit on adoption leave also currently unenforceable. This app shows the text as originally enacted, since Parliament has not yet formally rewritten the Act itself. If your situation involves parental, adoption, or commissioning parental leave, confirm the current interim entitlement with a labour law professional rather than relying on the section text shown here.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Adoption leave
body:
(1) An employee, who is an adoptive parent of a child who is below the age of two, is subject to subsection (6), entitled to-
(a) adoption leave of at least ten weeks consecutively; or
(b) the parental leave referred to in section 25A.
(2) An employee may commence adoption leave on the date-
(a) that the adoption order is granted; or
(b) that a child is placed in the care of a prospective adoptive parent by a competent court, pending the finalisation of an adoption order in respect of that child, whichever date occurs first.
(3) An employee must notify an employer in writing, unless the employee is unable to do so, of the date on which the employee intends to commence adoption leave and return to work after adoption leave.
(4) Notification in terms of subsection (3) must be given at least one month before the date referred to in subsection (2), or, if not reasonably practicable, as soon as reasonably practicable.
(5) The payment of adoption leave benefits will be determined by the Minister subject to the provisions of the Unemployment Insurance Act, 2001.
(6) If an adoption order is made in respect of two adoptive parents, only one of the adoptive parents may apply for the leave in terms of subsection (1)(a), and the other adoptive parent may apply for the parental leave in terms of section 25A.

IMPORTANT NOTE ON THIS SECTION: On 3 October 2025, the Constitutional Court (Van Wyk and Others v Minister of Employment and Labour) declared sections 25, 25A, 25B and 25C of this Act unconstitutional for discriminating between mothers, fathers, and different categories of parents. The Court suspended its order for 36 months to give Parliament time to properly rewrite these sections, but ordered an interim reading-in that applies immediately: broadly, two employed parents now share a pool of four months plus ten days of parental leave between them however they choose, and a single parent or the only employed parent in a relationship is entitled to the full four months. Section 25A is effectively removed under this interim scheme, and adoption/commissioning parental leave (sections 25B/25C) are aligned to the same shared structure, with the "under two years old" age limit on adoption leave also currently unenforceable. This app shows the text as originally enacted, since Parliament has not yet formally rewritten the Act itself. If your situation involves parental, adoption, or commissioning parental leave, confirm the current interim entitlement with a labour law professional rather than relying on the section text shown here.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Commissioning parental leave
body:
(1) An employee, who is a commissioning parent in a surrogate motherhood agreement, is subject to subsection (5), entitled to-
(a) commissioning parental leave of at least ten weeks consecutively; or
(b) the parental leave referred to in section 25A.
(2) An employee may commence commissioning parental leave on the date a child is born as a result of a surrogate motherhood agreement.
(3) An employee must notify an employer in writing, unless the employee is unable to do so, of the date on which the employee intends to commence commissioning parental leave and return to work after commissioning parental leave.
(4) Notification in terms of subsection (3) must be given at least one month before the child is expected to be born as a result of the surrogate motherhood agreement, or, if not reasonably practicable, as soon as reasonably practicable.
(5) If a child is born as a result of a surrogate motherhood agreement involving two commissioning parents, only one of the commissioning parents may apply for the leave in terms of subsection (1)(a), and the other commissioning parent may apply for the parental leave in terms of section 25A.

IMPORTANT NOTE ON THIS SECTION: On 3 October 2025, the Constitutional Court (Van Wyk and Others v Minister of Employment and Labour) declared sections 25, 25A, 25B and 25C of this Act unconstitutional for discriminating between mothers, fathers, and different categories of parents. The Court suspended its order for 36 months to give Parliament time to properly rewrite these sections, but ordered an interim reading-in that applies immediately: broadly, two employed parents now share a pool of four months plus ten days of parental leave between them however they choose, and a single parent or the only employed parent in a relationship is entitled to the full four months. Section 25A is effectively removed under this interim scheme, and adoption/commissioning parental leave (sections 25B/25C) are aligned to the same shared structure, with the "under two years old" age limit on adoption leave also currently unenforceable. This app shows the text as originally enacted, since Parliament has not yet formally rewritten the Act itself. If your situation involves parental, adoption, or commissioning parental leave, confirm the current interim entitlement with a labour law professional rather than relying on the section text shown here.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Daily wage payment
body:
(1) Despite section 9, an employer must pay an employee or a worker as defined in section 1 of the National Minimum Wage Act, 2018, who works for less than four hours on any day, for four hours' work on that day.
(2) This section applies to employees or workers who earn less than the earnings threshold set by the Minister in terms of section 6(3).

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Prohibited conduct by employer
body:
(1) An employer must not-
(a) require or accept any payment by or on behalf of an employee or potential employee in respect of the employment of, or the allocation of work to, any employee; or
(b) require an employee or potential employee to purchase any goods, products or services from the employer or from any business or person nominated by the employer.
(2) Subsection (1)(b) does not preclude a provision in a contract of employment or collective agreement in terms of which an employee is required to participate in a scheme involving the purchase of specific goods, products or services, if the purchase is not prohibited by any other statute and the employee receives a financial benefit from participating in the scheme, or the price of the goods, products or services provided through the scheme is fair and reasonable.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Definitions (Chapter Ten)
body: For the purposes of Chapter 10 (Monitoring, enforcement and legal proceedings), an employee includes a worker as defined in section 1 of the National Minimum Wage Act, 2018.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Claims for failure to pay any amount
body:
(1) Despite section 77, any employee or worker (as defined in the National Minimum Wage Act, 2018) may refer a dispute to the CCMA concerning failure to pay any amount owing under this Act, the National Minimum Wage Act, a contract of employment, a sectoral determination, or a collective agreement.
(2) This does not apply to employees or workers earning above the section 6(3) threshold.
(3) Such an employee or worker may instead institute a claim in the Labour Court, High Court, or (subject to jurisdiction) the Magistrates' Court or small claims court.
(4) The CCMA must appoint a Commissioner to attempt conciliation.
(5) The CCMA must commence arbitration immediately after certifying the dispute remains unresolved.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Fine for not complying with national minimum wage
body:
(1) Subject to section 76, a fine for paying an employee less than the national minimum wage is the greater of twice the value of the underpayment or twice the employee's monthly wage.
(2) For second or further non-compliances, the fine is the greater of thrice the value of the underpayment or thrice the employee's monthly wage.
(3) The Minister may issue guidelines on determining whether a non-compliance is a second or further one.
(4) The Department must maintain and publish quarterly, on its website, a list of employers issued compliance orders.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Powers of Labour Court
body: The Labour Court may make any appropriate order, including condoning a late filing or referral, reviewing the performance of any function under this Act, making a reasonable determination on a contract of employment matter (including specific performance, damages, or compensation), imposing a fine under Schedule Two, and dealing with any matter necessary or incidental to its functions.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Rights of employees
body:
(1) Every employee has the right to make a complaint to a trade union representative, official, or labour inspector about an alleged failure to comply with this Act or the National Minimum Wage Act, 2018; discuss conditions of employment with colleagues, the employer, or anyone else; refuse to comply with an instruction contrary to this Act, the National Minimum Wage Act, or a sectoral determination; refuse to agree to a contrary term or condition; inspect relevant employment records; participate in proceedings under this Act; and request a trade union representative or labour inspector to inspect relevant records.
(2) Every trade union representative has the right, at an employee's request, to inspect records relating to that employee's employment.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Protection of rights
body:
(1) In this section, "employee" includes a former employee or an applicant for employment.
(2) No person may discriminate against, or require, prevent, or threaten to prevent an employee from exercising a right under this Part, or prejudice an employee because of a past, present, or anticipated exercise of such a right, a lawful refusal, or a lawful disclosure.
(3) No person may favour or promise to favour an employee in exchange for not exercising a right under this Part, though this does not preclude a settlement agreement.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Procedure for disputes
body:
(1) A dispute about the interpretation or application of this Part may be referred in writing to the CCMA by any party, including a labour inspector.
(3) The CCMA must attempt conciliation.
(4) If unresolved, any party may refer it to the CCMA for arbitration.
(5) The relevant Labour Relations Act dispute-resolution provisions apply with necessary changes.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Deeming of persons as employees
body:
(1) The Minister may, on the advice of the Commission and by Gazette notice, deem a category of persons to be employees for the whole or part of this Act, another employment law (other than the Unemployment Insurance Act), or a sectoral determination, or to be contributors for purposes of the Unemployment Insurance Act.
(2) Before issuing such a notice, the Minister must publish a draft in the Gazette and invite public comment.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Presumption as to who is employee
body:
(1) A person who works for, or renders services to, another person is presumed, until the contrary is proved, to be an employee if any of the following factors are present: their manner or hours of work are controlled by another person, they form part of that organisation, they have worked an average of at least 40 hours per month over the last three months, they are economically dependent on the other person, they are provided with tools or work equipment, or they only work for or render services to one person.
(2) This presumption does not apply to a person earning above the section 6(3) threshold.
(3) Where a proposed or existing work arrangement involves persons earning at or below that threshold, any party may approach the CCMA for an advisory award on whether they are employees.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Duration of employment
body:
(1) Previous employment with the same employer must be counted toward an employee's length of employment for any provision of this Act if the break between periods was less than one year.
(2) Any payment made or leave granted during a previous period of employment must be taken into account in determining the employee's current entitlement.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Delegation
body:
(1) The Minister may in writing delegate or assign any power or duty under this Act to the Director-General or a public service employee of assistant director rank or higher, except the powers under sections 6(3), 55(1), 60, 83, 87, 95(2), and the power to make regulations.
(2) A delegation does not limit the Minister's own authority to exercise the power.
(4) The Minister may withdraw a delegation or any decision made under it at any time.
(5) The Director-General may similarly delegate Chapter Ten powers/duties to a departmental employee of assistant director rank or higher.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Regulations
body:
(1) The Minister may, by Gazette notice after consulting the Commission, make regulations on any matter necessary or expedient to achieve this Act's objects.
(2) A regulation regarding state revenue or expenditure requires the Minister of Finance's concurrence.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Codes of Good Practice
body:
(1) The Minister, after consulting NEDLAC, must issue a Code of Good Practice on the Arrangement of Working Time and one on the Protection of Employees during Pregnancy and after Birth, may issue other codes, and may change or replace any code.
(2) Any code or change must be published in the Gazette.
(3) Anyone interpreting or applying this Act must take relevant codes into account.
(4) A code may provide that it must be taken into account in applying or interpreting any employment law.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Minister's power to add and change footnotes
body: The Minister may, by Gazette notice, add to, change, or replace any footnote in this Act.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Representation of employees or employers
body:
(1) A registered trade union or employers' organisation may act in its own interest, on behalf of a member, or in the interest of a member, in any dispute to which a member is a party.
(2) It is entitled to be a party to proceedings under this Act if one of its members is a party.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Confidentiality
body:
(1) It is an offence to disclose information acquired while exercising a power or duty under this Act relating to another person's financial or business affairs, except as needed to perform an employment-law function, for the proper administration of this Act, or for the administration of justice.
(2) This does not prevent disclosure of an employer's compliance or non-compliance with any employment law.
(3) A medical examination record must be kept confidential, disclosed only per medical ethics, if required by law or court order, or with the employee's written consent.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Answers not to be used in criminal prosecutions
body: No answer given to a section 53 investigation question or a section 66 labour inspector question may be used against that person in criminal proceedings, except for a charge of perjury or making a false statement.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Obstruction, undue influence and fraud
body: It is an offence to obstruct or improperly influence a person performing a function under this Act, obtain a prescribed document by fraud or a false/forged document, pretend to be a labour inspector or other official, refuse or fail to answer a lawful question, refuse or fail to comply with a lawful request or order, or hinder or obstruct a labour inspector or other official.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Penalties
body:
(1) Any magistrates' court has jurisdiction to impose a penalty for an offence under this Act.
(2) Maximum terms of imprisonment on conviction: section 33A - 3 years; section 43 - 6 years; section 44 - 6 years; section 46 - 6 years; section 48 - 6 years; section 90(1) and (3) - 1 year; section 92 - 1 year.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: This Act binds the State
body: This Act binds the State except in so far as criminal liability is concerned.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Transitional arrangements and amendment and repeal of laws
body:
(1) Schedule Three applies to the transition from other laws to this Act.
(2) The Minister may add to or change Schedule Three to regulate this transition.
(3) Any addition or change must be tabled in the National Assembly and takes effect if not rejected within 14 days, on Gazette publication.
(5) The laws listed in Schedule Four are repealed to the extent indicated.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Short title
body: This is the Basic Conditions of Employment Act, 1997.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Payment of contributions to benefit funds
body:
(1) For the purposes of this section, a benefit fund is a pension, provident, retirement, medical aid or similar fund.
(2) An employer that deducts from an employee's remuneration any amount for payment to a benefit fund must pay the amount to the fund within seven days of the deduction being made.
(3) Any contribution that an employer is required to make to a benefit fund on behalf of an employee, that is not deducted from the employee's remuneration, must be paid to the fund within seven days of the end of the period in respect of which the payment is made.
(4) This section does not affect any obligation on an employer in terms of the rules of a benefit fund to make any payment within a shorter period than that required by subsections (2) or (3).

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Burden of proof
body:
In any proceeding in terms of this Part-
(a) an employee who alleges that a right or protection conferred by this Part has been infringed, must prove the facts of the conduct said to constitute such infringement; and
(b) the party who allegedly engaged in the conduct in question must then prove that the conduct did not infringe any provision of this Part.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Temporary employment services
body:
(1) For the purposes of this Act, a person whose services have been procured for, or provided to, a client by a temporary employment service is the employee of that temporary employment service, and the temporary employment service is that person's employer.
(2) Despite subsection (1), a person who is an independent contractor is not an employee of a temporary employment service, nor is the temporary employment service the employer of that person.
(3) The temporary employment service and the client are jointly and severally liable if the temporary employment service, in respect of any employee who provides services to that client, does not comply with this Act or a sectoral determination.

collection: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997
title: Certificate of service

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Jurisdiction of Labour Court
body:
(1) The Labour Court has exclusive jurisdiction to determine any dispute about the interpretation or application of any provision of this Act except where this Act provides otherwise.
(2) The Labour Court has no jurisdiction in respect of offences in terms of this Act.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: No discrimination against employees who exercise rights

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Safety equipment not to be interfered with
body:
Unless specifically authorised by the employer, no person-
(a) other than an inspector acting in terms of section 50, may remove personal protective equipment from a mine, or cause that equipment to be removed;
(b) other than an inspector acting in terms of section 50, may remove anything that is provided in the interest of health or safety, or cause that equipment to be removed; or
(c) may alter, damage, misuse, render ineffective or interfere with anything that is provided in the interest of health or safety, or cause that equipment to be altered, damaged, misused, rendered ineffective or interfered with.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Juvenile employment underground prohibited
body:
(1) No person may cause or permit an employee under the age of 18 years to work underground at a mine.
(2) No employee under the age of 18 years may work underground at a mine.
(3) Despite subsections (1) and (2), an employee under the age of 18 years but over the age of 16 years may work underground as part of vocational education or training.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Negligent act or omission
body:
(1) Any person who, by a negligent act or by a negligent omission, causes serious injury or serious illness to a person at a mine, commits an offence.
(2) Any person, other than an employer or employee, who, by a negligent act or by a negligent omission, endangers the health or safety of a person at a mine, commits an offence.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Criminal liability
body:
(1) An employer, Chief Executive Officer, manager, agent or employee commits an offence if he or she contravenes or fails to comply with the provisions of this Act thereby causing a person's death, or serious injury or illness to a person.
(2) If a Chief Executive Officer, manager, agent or employee of the employer commits an offence by performing or omitting to perform an act and such performance or omission would have constituted an offence had it been done by the employer, that employer is equally committing an offence if the act or omission fell within the scope of the authority or employment of the Chief Executive Officer, manager, agent or employee concerned and the employer connived at or permitted the performance or omission, or did not take all reasonable steps to prevent it.
(3) For the purposes of subsection (1), issuing instructions prohibiting the performance or omission is not in itself sufficient proof that all reasonable steps were taken to prevent it; the defence of ignorance or mistake by an accused cannot be admitted; and the defence that the death, injury, illness or endangerment was caused by an act or omission falling within the scope of another individual's authority or employment may not be admitted.

Note: this section was inserted by section 26 of Act 74 of 2008, but as of the source used to build this entry, it had not yet been brought into effect by proclamation - confirm its current commencement status if relying on it.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Breach of confidence
body:
(1) Any person who discloses any information that they acquired in the performance of a function in terms of this Act and that relates to the financial and business affairs of an employer or any other person who employs employees, commits an offence.
(2) Subsection (1) does not apply if the information was disclosed to enable a person to perform a function in terms of this Act, must be disclosed in terms of this Act, any other law or an order of court, or was disclosed to a health and safety representative or health and safety committee in terms of Chapter 3.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Hindering administration of this Act
body: Any person who hinders, opposes, obstructs or unduly influences any person who is performing a function in terms of this Act commits an offence.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Falsifying documents
body: Any person who obtains or attempts to obtain a prescribed certificate of competency by means of fraud, dishonesty, false pretences or the presentation or submission of a false or forged document commits an offence.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Failure to attend when summoned
body: A person commits an offence who, having been instructed or summoned to attend an inquiry, without sufficient cause fails to appear at the time and place specified or fails to remain in attendance until excused by the presiding person; attends as required but without sufficient cause fails to comply with an instruction to produce a document or item, or refuses to be sworn or to make an affirmation; or attends as required and having been sworn or having made an affirmation, without sufficient cause fails to answer any question fully and to the best of that person's ability, or gives evidence knowing or believing it to be false.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Magistrate's court has jurisdiction to impose penalties
body: Despite anything to the contrary contained in any other law, a magistrate's court has jurisdiction to impose any penalty provided for in this Act.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Certain compensation to employers prohibited
body:
(1) Any employer who deducts from the earnings of an employee any amount or receives any amount from him or her to compensate the employer directly or indirectly for any amount which the employer is liable to pay in terms of this Act, shall be liable to a penalty specified in subsection (2).
(2) The Commissioner shall, in addition to any penalty he or she may impose, direct the employer to pay to the Commissioner within a specified period and in instalments or otherwise as the Commissioner may determine, such amount as he or she has received contrary to the provisions of subsection (1).
(3) The Commissioner shall pay the amount received by him or her in terms of subsection (2) to the employee from whose earnings that amount has been deducted or from whom the amount has been received.
(4) Upon request by the employer, the Commissioner may at any time, on good cause shown, extend the period within which the amount referred to in subsection (2) is payable or amend the amount of the instalments.
(5) The provisions of section 93E apply with necessary alterations to an employer who does not comply with the provisions of this section.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Calculation of compensation (occupational diseases)
body:
(1) Compensation for a disease referred to in section 65(1) shall be calculated on the basis of the earnings of the employee calculated with necessary changes required by the context, in accordance with the provisions of section 63 and the disablement of the employee at the time of the commencement of the disease or such earlier date as the Commissioner may determine, if it is proved to his or her satisfaction that the employee was suffering from the disease at an earlier date, whichever earnings are favourable to the employee.
(2) If an employee is no longer in employment at the time of the commencement of the said disease, the employee's earnings shall be calculated on the basis of the earnings that the employee would probably have been earning had the employee still been employed.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Compensation Fund to provide rehabilitation
body:
(1) Subject to the provisions of this Act, the Compensation Fund, the employer individually liable or licensee as the case may be, must provide facilities, services and benefits aimed at rehabilitating employees suffering from occupational injuries or diseases to return to their work or to reduce any disability resulting from their injuries or diseases.
(2) The rehabilitation benefits provided in subsection (1) may consist of-
(a) clinical rehabilitation and the provision of assistive devices for the purpose of physical and psychological recovery of the employee and to reduce any disability resulting from an occupational injury or disease;
(b) vocational rehabilitation to assist an employee to maintain employment, obtain employment, regain or acquire vocational independence; and
(c) social rehabilitation to assist in restoring an employee's independence and social integration to the maximum extent practicable.

This is a new chapter (Chapter VIIA) inserted by the Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Amendment Act 10 of 2022, now in force.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Consultation of representatives of medical authorities by Commissioner
body: The Commissioner may consult with the Health Professions Council of South Africa, registered Medical Associations and any other representative medical authority concerning matters connected with or arising out of the application of the provisions of this Act with regard to medical aid, and may for that purpose disclose any information relating to a matter in respect of which the views of the Health Professions Council of South Africa, the registered Medical Associations or other representative medical authority are required.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Assessment to be paid by employer to Compensation Fund
body:
(1) An assessment shall be paid by an employer to the Compensation Fund within 30 days after the date of the notice of assessment or, with the approval of the Commissioner, in such instalments and at such times and on such conditions as the Commissioner may determine.
(2) Interest is payable on an overdue assessment at a rate determined by the Commissioner, which shall not exceed the prevailing standard rate of interest as defined in the Prescribed Rate of Interest Act, 1975 (Act No. 55 of 1975).

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Term of office of Board
body:
(1) The members of the Board appointed by the Minister shall-
(a) be appointed for a period not exceeding four years; and
(b) not serve for more than two terms.
(2) When a member of the Board vacates office for any reason, the Minister shall fill the vacancy in accordance with subsection (1) for the unexpired portion of that period.
(3) Members of the Board shall be paid the prescribed remuneration and travelling and subsistence allowance out of the finances of the Compensation Fund.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Secretariat of Board
body: The Commissioner shall, in consultation with the Board, provide the necessary resources and secretariat to enable the Board to fulfil its functions.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Disqualifications of Board members
body: A person may not be appointed as a member of the Board, or remain a member of the Board, if that person is an unrehabilitated insolvent or becomes insolvent resulting in sequestration of their estate; has been declared mentally ill by a competent court; has been convicted of theft, fraud, forgery, perjury or any other dishonest act; has been convicted of any other offence committed after the Constitution took effect and sentenced to imprisonment without the option of a fine; has been removed from a position of trust for misconduct involving fraud, misappropriation, or dishonesty; is otherwise disqualified from serving on a board under the Companies Act, 2008; or has an interest in a business that could conflict with the proper performance of the Board's functions.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Resignation and removal from office
body:
(1) A member of the Board may resign by giving the Minister one month's prior written notice, or less with the Minister's approval.
(2) The Minister may remove a member from the Board for serious misconduct, permanent incapacity, being absent from three consecutive Board meetings without prior permission (unless just cause is shown), or engaging in an activity that could undermine the Board's functions.
(3) The Minister shall prescribe the procedure for the removal of Board members.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Constitution of Board
body:
(1) The Board shall be appointed by the Minister and shall consist of-
(a) an independent chairperson who has no vote; and
(b) 16 voting members-
(i) of which five members and two alternate members are nominated by NEDLAC to represent organised labour;
(ii) of which five members and two alternate members are nominated by NEDLAC to represent business;
(iii) of which five members and two alternate members are appointed by the Minister to represent the interests of the state; and
(iv) which includes the Commissioner by virtue of his or her office.
(4) If a member of the Board vacates office before the expiry of his or her period of office, the Minister must appoint another member to fill the vacancy for the unexpired portion of that period.
(5) The Minister may, on the recommendation of the Board, appoint additional Board members with relevant qualifications, skills and expertise for the efficient governance of the Fund.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Board functions
body:
(2) The Board may at the request of the Commissioner advise him or her on the performance of any aspect of the Commissioner's functions in terms of this Act.
(3) The Board must within three months after the appointment of its members, prepare and adopt a Board Charter.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Valuation of Compensation Fund
body: (1) The assets and liabilities of the Compensation Fund shall from time to time, as the Commissioner may consider necessary, but in any event at intervals of not more than three years, be valued by an actuary appointed by the Commissioner to determine the sufficiency of the Compensation Fund.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Investment of Compensation Fund monies
body: (2) The Commissioner may transfer any part of the monies in the Compensation Fund and the reserve fund to the Public Investment Corporation for investment.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Accounts and financial statements
body:
(1) The Commissioner shall keep such accounts, including an account with a bank contemplated in the Banks Act, 1990, and the Public Finance Management Act, 1999, and records as are necessary for the exercise of proper control over the Compensation Fund and the reserve fund, and shall prepare annual financial statements made up to the last day of the financial year, showing in all necessary detail the assets and liabilities and the revenue and expenditure of the funds.
(3) The Commissioner shall submit to the Minister the annual financial statement together with the annual report and any other relevant documentation as provided for in section 55 of the Public Finance Management Act, 1999.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Special circumstances in which Commissioner may refuse award
body: (b) if, in the opinion of the Commissioner, the death or the disablement was caused, prolonged or aggravated, by the employee unreasonably refusing to submit to medical aid or rehabilitation programmes in respect of any injury or disease, whether caused by the accident or existing before the accident.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
