title: Licence to carry out business of Compensation Fund
body:
(1) The Minister may, for such period and subject to such conditions as he or she may determine, issue a licence to carry on the business of insurance of employers against their liabilities to employees in terms of this Act to a licensee: Provided that the Minister may order that the licensee deposit securities considered by the Director-General to be sufficient to cover the liabilities of the licensee in terms of this Act.
(4) If the Minister is satisfied that the whole or any portion of such security is no longer necessary and that the licensee concerned is not in a position to incur a liability payable therefrom, the Minister shall cause such security, or portion thereof, to be returned to such licensee.
(5) If a licensee has deposited with the Compensation Fund any such security and thereafter fails to meet in full any of its liabilities in terms of this Act, or is placed in liquidation, then, notwithstanding the provisions of any other law, such security shall vest in the Compensation Fund for the purpose of the liabilities of the licensee in terms of this Act.
(7) Any licensee issued with a licence in terms of this Act shall be accountable to the Minister.
(8) All such securities mentioned in subsections (1) and (2) shall be deposited with the Compensation Fund or its nominee.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Inquiry by Commissioner into accident
body:
(1) The Commissioner shall, after having received notice of an accident or having learned in some other way that an employee has met with an accident, make such inquiry as he or she may deem necessary for purposes of determining liability in terms of this Act.
(3) The Commissioner shall, at the request of an injured employee or the employer, furnish such information as the Commissioner may deem necessary to enable that employee or employer to comply with the provisions of this Act.
(4) An employer who fails to comply with the provisions of this section shall be liable to a penalty of 10 per cent plus interest on actual earnings declared to the Compensation Fund.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Duty of employee to furnish information
body:
(1) An employee who has met with an accident shall, when reporting the accident or thereafter at the request of the employer or Commissioner, furnish such information and documents as prescribed and any such documents that may be requested.
(3) If the employee independently obtained a medical report in terms of this section at his or her own costs, the Commissioner must reimburse such medical expenses in full, where the Commissioner has received and accepted the report.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Employee to submit to medical examination and rehabilitation
body:
(1A) An employee contemplated in subsection (1) shall, if required to do so, submit himself or herself to an examination for purposes of rehabilitation.
(2) Such expenses incurred by the employee to comply with the provisions of this section as the Commissioner may deem necessary and reasonable, and the prescribed remuneration for a medical examination or rehabilitation in terms of this section, shall be paid by the party requiring the examination or rehabilitation.
(3) If, according to the determination of a designated medical practitioner, the employee is not able to attend the medical examination or rehabilitation in terms of subsections (1) and (1A), such designated medical practitioner or the employee shall inform the party requiring the examination thereof, and the designated medical practitioner shall then examine the employee at a time and place as agreed upon.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Commencement of monthly pension
body: Notwithstanding any provision in this Act, monthly pension shall commence from the date on which a medical practitioner certifies that an employee has reached the maximum medical intervention.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Review of assessment of disablement
body:
(1)(d) of an engineer appointed to be in general charge of the machinery, or of a person appointed to assist such engineer.
(3)(c) The provisions of sections 6, 7, 45, 46 and 93D shall, in consideration of applications in terms of this section, apply mutatis mutandis in respect of such an application.
(6) The presiding officer may in any proceedings in terms of this section make an order as to costs subject to the provisions of section 46(7).

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Compensation for occupational diseases
body:
(1)(a) that the employee has contracted a disease mentioned in Schedule 3 and that such disease has arisen out of and in the course of his or her employment; or
(2) If an employee has contracted a disease referred to in subsection (1) and the Commissioner is of the opinion that the recovery of the employee is being delayed or that his or her temporary total disablement is being prolonged by reason of some other disease of which the employee is suffering, the Commissioner may approve medical costs also for such other disease for so long as he or she may deem necessary.
(5) For the purposes of this Act the commencement of a disease referred to in subsection (1) shall be deemed to be the date on which a medical practitioner diagnosed that disease for the first time or such earlier date as the Commissioner may determine if it is more favourable to the employee.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Conveyance of injured and diseased employee
body:
(2) The Commissioner or the employer individually liable or licensee concerned, as the case may be, may pay the reasonable cost incurred in respect of that conveyance.
(3) Any employer who fails to comply with subsection (1) shall be liable to a penalty equal to the full cost of conveyance.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Medical costs and reopening of claims
body:
(3) Notwithstanding the provision of subsection (2), the medical practitioner may, after the claim has been finalised or the relevant period has lapsed, apply for reopening of the claim and payment of further medical costs.
(4)(a) No third party will be allowed to transact with the Compensation Fund unless they are registered with the Compensation Fund in the manner as prescribed.
(b) All third parties that are already transacting with the Compensation Fund must register with the Compensation Fund within six months after the commencement of the Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Amendment Act, 2022.
(5) For the purpose of this section, a third party means any entity that transacts with the Fund with the aim of assisting either the employee, employer, medical service provider or pensioner with the processing of claims at the Compensation Fund.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Submission of medical report
body:
(1) A medical practitioner must furnish a medical report within 14 days of first examining an injured employee or diagnosing an occupational disease.
(2) Further reports must be furnished on request.
(3) Payment of medical aid costs may be deferred until a satisfactory report is furnished.
(4) No remuneration is payable for completing such reports.
(5) A medical practitioner must give the employee or dependant a copy of the report on request.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Tariff of fees for medical aid
body: (2) The tariff of fees for medical aid shall be determined after consultation with the Health Professions Council of South Africa and registered Medical Associations.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Reimbursement of medical costs
body: (2)(c) the Commissioner may reimburse an employer who is not individually liable such costs out of the Compensation Fund or reduce his or her assessment to such an extent as the Commissioner may deem equitable.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Assessment of employers

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Rebate on assessment
body: (3) If the accident record of an employer during a particular period is in the opinion of the Commissioner more favourable than those of employers in comparable businesses, or if the employer is participating in the rehabilitation of employees as prescribed, the Commissioner may give such employer a rebate on any assessment paid or payable by him or her.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Mandators and contractors
body:
(1) If a person (the mandator) in the course of or for the purposes of his business enters into an agreement with any other person (the contractor) for the execution by or under the supervision of the contractor of the whole or any part of any work undertaken by the mandator, the contractor shall, in respect of his employees employed in the execution of the work concerned, register as an employer in accordance with the provisions of this Act and pay the necessary assessments. If a contractor fails so to register or pay any assessment, the said employees of the contractor shall be deemed to be the employees of the mandator, and the mandator shall pay the assessments in respect of those employees.
(2) If a mandator has paid an assessment or compensation for which he would not have been liable but for the provisions of subsection (1), such mandator may recover that assessment or compensation from the contractor.
(3) If a mandator has in terms of this section paid an assessment or compensation to the Commissioner, he may set off the amount so paid by him against his debt to the contractor.

Note: the same arrangement applies one level down between a contractor and any sub-contractor it engages, with the contractor standing in the mandator's position.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Appointment of inspectors
body:
(1) The Commissioner may appoint any person as an inspector for purposes of this Act.
(2) Any person appointed under subsection (1) shall perform the functions in terms of this Act, subject to the direction and control of the Commissioner.
(3) The Commissioner shall provide each inspector with a signed certificate in the prescribed form stating that the person is an inspector, which legislation an inspector may monitor and enforce, and which of the functions an inspector may perform.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Functions of inspectors
body: An inspector appointed in terms of this Act may promote, monitor and enforce compliance with this Act by advising employees and employers of their rights and obligations, conducting inspections to ensure compliance, investigating complaints made to the Commissioner, issuing compliance orders, and performing any other function related to their functions under this Act.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Powers of entry
body:
(1) An inspector may enter a home or any other place only with the consent of the owner or occupier, or authorised to do so in writing in terms of subsection (2).
(2) The Labour Court may issue such an authorisation only on written application and on notice by an inspector who states under oath or affirmation the reasons for the need to enter a place in order to monitor or enforce compliance with this Act.
(3) If it is practical to do so, the employer and a trade union representative shall be notified that an inspector is present at a workplace and of the reason for the inspection.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Powers to question and inspect
body:
(1) In order to monitor or enforce compliance with this Act, an inspector may require a person to disclose information (including under oath), inspect and question about any record or document, copy or remove records/documents, require production of records/documents, inspect and if necessary remove any article, substance or machinery, inspect or question about work performed, and perform any other function necessary for monitoring or enforcing compliance.
(2) An inspector may be accompanied by an interpreter, a member of the South African Police Services and any other person reasonably required to assist in conducting the inspection.
(3) An inspector shall produce their certificate on request, provide a receipt for anything removed, and return anything removed within a month.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Co-operation with inspectors
body:
(1) Any person who is questioned by an inspector shall answer all questions truthfully and honestly.
(2) Every employer and employee shall co-operate with the inspectors to perform functions effectively.
(3) No answer by any person to a question by an authorised person or an inspector conducting an investigation or inspection may be used against that person in any criminal proceedings, except proceedings in respect of a charge of perjury or making a false statement.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Compliance orders
body:
(1) An inspector who has reasonable grounds to believe that an employer has not complied with a provision of this Act may issue a compliance order.
(2) A compliance order must set out the employer's name and the location of every relevant workplace, the provision not complied with and details of the non-compliance, required steps and timeframe, and the maximum fine that may be imposed.
(3) An inspector shall deliver a copy of the compliance order to the employer, and to each affected employee (or their representative, if impractical to reach each employee).
(4) An employer shall comply with the compliance order within the time period stated in the order.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Compliance order made order of court
body: The Commissioner may apply to the Labour Court for a compliance order to be made an order of court if the employer has not complied.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Staff to assist Director-General
body:
(1) The Minister shall, subject to such conditions as he or she may determine, in order to assist the Director-General in the performance of his or her functions in terms of or under this Act and subject to the laws governing the public service, appoint an officer to be called the Compensation Commissioner, and such other officers and employees as the Minister or an officer designated by him or her may deem necessary.
(2) The Commissioner, and the officers and employees, shall be remunerated out of the National Revenue Fund, which shall be reimbursed out of the Compensation Fund for the expenditure concerned.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Delegation of powers and assignment of duties by Director-General
body:
(1) The Director-General may, subject to such conditions as he or she may determine, delegate any of his or her powers or assign any of his or her duties to the Commissioner, or an officer or employee, and may at any time cancel any such delegation or assignment.
(2) A delegation or assignment under subsection (1) shall not divest the Director-General of the power delegated or duty assigned, and he or she may at any time amend or set aside any decision made thereunder, and shall not prevent the exercise of the power or the performance of the duty concerned by the Director-General himself or herself.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Functions of Director-General
body:
(1) Subject to the provisions of this Act, the Director-General shall inquire into accidents and occupational diseases, adjudicate on claims and other matters coming before him for decision, issue an order for the payment of compensation, decide whether a person is an employee, employer, mandator or contractor, decide questions relating to the right to compensation and calculation of earnings, decide whether a person is a dependant of an employee, decide upon the need for and sufficiency of medical aid, decide upon assessment matters, administer the Compensation Fund and reserve fund, recover amounts due to the Fund, submit an annual report to the Minister, record statistics on accidents and diseases, and institute inquiries as may be prescribed.
(2) The Director-General may enter into agreements for the performance of particular tasks, found or subsidise bodies whose objects include accident prevention or promoting employee health/safety or rehabilitation, purchase shares in such bodies, and apply unclaimed compensation for the general welfare of injured employees.
(3) The Commissioner shall receive notices of accidents and occupational diseases, claims for compensation, medical reports and accounts, objections, applications, returns of earnings and payments due to the Compensation Fund, and by notice in the Gazette prescribe relevant rules and forms.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Power of Director-General to acquire and alienate immovable property and to raise money
body:
(1) The Director-General may with the approval of the Minister raise money by way of loans, and purchase or otherwise acquire immovable property, and alienate such property.
(2) Immovable property acquired shall be held in the name of the Director-General in trust for the Compensation Fund.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Powers of Director-General regarding witnesses and subpoenas
body:
(1) The Director-General may subpoena any person able to give information concerning an inquiry, or suspected of having a relevant book, document or thing, to appear before him for interrogation or to produce it, and may retain it for further investigation. Such an inquiry shall take place in public unless the Director-General orders otherwise.
(2) The Director-General may administer an oath or accept an affirmation from such a person, and interrogate them or order production of documents.
(3) A person who fails to attend as subpoenaed, refuses to be sworn, refuses to answer, refuses to produce a document, or hinders the Director-General commits an offence.
(4) A person who makes a false statement under oath commits an offence liable to the penalty for perjury.
(5) The law of privilege applicable to court witnesses applies at such an inquiry.
(6) The Director-General may pay a subpoenaed person's reasonable loss or expense from the Compensation Fund.
(7) The Director-General may delegate functions under this section to an assessor, officer, employee, or medical practitioner.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Functions of commissioner
body: The commissioner shall receive notices of accidents and occupational diseases, claims for compensation, medical reports and accounts, objections, applications, returns of earnings and payments due to the Compensation Fund, and by notice in the Gazette prescribe the rules referred to in section 56(3)(c), the forms to be used, and particulars to be furnished.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Powers of authorized person
body:
(1) The Director-General may authorize any assessor, officer, employee, or medical practitioner to investigate any necessary matter.
(2) An authorized person shall be furnished with a certificate to that effect.
(3) An authorized person may, without previous notice, enter any premises with an interpreter, assistant, or police officer; question any person there; order production of relevant documents; seize evidence; examine and copy documents; and order an employee to appear for questioning.
(4) An authorized person must produce their certificate on demand.
(5) Falsely holding oneself out as an authorized person, refusing to answer or comply, or hindering an authorized person is an offence.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Assessors
body:
(1) The Minister may, after consulting the Board, appoint assessors to assist the Director-General in hearing objections under section 91.
(2) Assessors must represent the interests of employees and employers respectively.
(3) The number representing employees shall equal the number representing employers.
(4) The Minister may also appoint medical assessors.
(5) An assessor is appointed for a period and conditions the Minister determines, and may be removed for misconduct, inability to perform functions, or no longer representing the relevant interest.
(6) Assessors are paid prescribed remuneration and allowances from the Compensation Fund.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Compensation payable to assessors
body:
(1) If an assessor meets with an accident while performing their functions, resulting in injury, illness, or death, they or their dependants are entitled to compensation as if they were an employee.
(2) Compensation is paid by the Director-General out of the Compensation Fund.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Compensation Board
body: There is hereby established a board to be known as the Compensation Board.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Meetings of Board
body:
(1) The Board shall meet at times and places determined by the chairman.
(2) If six or more members request a meeting in writing with reasons, the Director-General shall convene one within 21 days.
(3) A quorum is nine members.
(4) A decision of more than 75 per cent of members present at a meeting is the Board's decision.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Compensation Fund establishment
body:
(1) There is hereby established a fund to be known as the Compensation Fund.
(2) The Compensation Fund consists of vested moneys, employer assessments, amounts paid to the Director-General, penalties and fines, investment interest, transfers from the reserve fund, section 88 payments, and other entitled amounts.
(3) The former Workmen's Compensation Act accident fund ceased to exist on this Act's commencement, with its assets and liabilities transferred to the Compensation Fund.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Application of Compensation Fund
body:
(1) The Compensation Fund, under the Director-General's control, is applied to paying compensation and medical aid where no one else is liable, maintaining the reserve fund, paying performance-of-functions expenses, reimbursing the National Revenue Fund, paying assessor remuneration, paying medical examination costs, paying witness fees, and other expenditure incurred administering this Act.
(2) The Director-General may transfer any surplus to the reserve fund.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Reserve fund
body:
(1) There is hereby established a reserve fund, consisting of cash or investments or both.
(2) Its amount is determined by the Director-General.
(3) Its objects are to provide for unforeseen demands on the Compensation Fund and to stabilise assessment tariffs.
(4) Payments out of it require the Director-General's authorisation.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Income of funds exempt from tax
body: The income of the Compensation Fund and the reserve fund, including investment income, is exempt from income tax.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Accidents outside Republic
body:
(1) If an employer carries on business chiefly in the Republic and an employee ordinarily employed in the Republic meets with an accident while temporarily employed outside the Republic, that employee is entitled to compensation as if the accident happened in the Republic, calculated on the earnings the employee would have received if they had remained in the Republic. This ceases to apply after 12 continuous months abroad, save by agreement.
(2) An employee resident in the Republic who meets with an accident on the continental shelf is entitled to compensation as if it happened in the Republic.
(3) If an employer carries on business chiefly outside the Republic and an employee ordinarily employed outside the Republic meets with an accident while temporarily employed in the Republic, that employee is not entitled to compensation unless the employer previously agreed with the Commissioner that the employee would be covered and paid the necessary assessments. After 12 continuous months in the Republic, such an employee is deemed ordinarily employed there.
(4) Where an employee could claim compensation under both this Act and the law of another state, they must elect, by written notice, which law to claim under.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Application of Act to seamen and airmen
body: This Act applies to a seaman or airman while employed on a South African ship or aircraft, or while employed in the Republic on any other ship or aircraft.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Accidents during training for or performance of emergency services
body: If an employee meets with an accident while being trained (with their employer's consent) in organised first aid, ambulance or rescue work, fire-fighting or other emergency service; while engaged in such work on their employer's premises; or while engaged (with their employer's consent) in such work on other premises, the accident is deemed to have arisen out of and in the course of their employment.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Special circumstances in which Director-General may make award
body: If it appears that an employee's contract of service, apprenticeship, or learnership is invalid, the Director-General may deal with a compensation claim as if the contract had been valid at the time of the accident.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Employee requiring constant help
body: If the injury causes disablement such that the employee cannot perform essential life activities without another person's constant help, the Director-General may grant an allowance towards the cost of that help, in addition to other benefits.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Liability for payment of compensation
body: If an employee is entitled to compensation, the Director-General, the employer individually liable, or the licensee concerned, as the case may be, is liable for its payment.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Security for payment of compensation and cost of medical aid by employers individually liable
body:
(1) The Director-General may order an employer individually liable to deposit sufficient securities to cover the employer's liabilities under this Act.
(2) If such an employer fails to meet their liabilities, the Director-General may apply the security to pay them, depositing any unused balance in the Compensation Fund for future liabilities of that employer.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Compensation may not be alienated or reduced
body:
(1) Compensation may not be ceded, pledged, attached, or executed under a court judgment, or set off against any debt of the person entitled to it.
(2) The Director-General or licensee may pay compensation owed to an employee in whole or part to the employer, to the extent the employer has already made payments to the employee for the same disablement.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Cession or relinquishment of benefits void
body: Any agreement provision, whether existing at this Act's commencement or concluded afterward, in which an employee cedes or relinquishes (or purports to) any right to benefits under this Act, is void.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Compensation not to form part of deceased employee's estate
body: Compensation owing due to an employee's death does not form part of their estate.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Threats and compulsion
body: Any person who threatens an employee, or in any manner compels or influences an employee to do something resulting in or aimed at depriving that employee of their right to benefits under this Act, commits an offence.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Consideration of claim
body:
(1) The Director-General shall consider and adjudicate a compensation claim, carrying out any investigation necessary, or formally hearing the claim.
(2) If a formal hearing is decided upon, notice of date, time, and place is given to the claimant and employer.
(3) The Director-General may subpoena any person, including the claimant and employer, needed at a formal hearing.
(6) The Director-General may adjourn a formal hearing to a determined date, time and place.
(7) The Director-General must keep a record of formal hearing proceedings, obtainable by any person on payment of prescribed fees.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Appearance of parties
body:
(1) Every party to a compensation claim, or their representative, may appear before the Director-General at a formal hearing, and the Director-General may designate someone to investigate, attend, cross-examine, and present arguments.
(2) Only a legal practitioner is entitled to fees or remuneration beyond expenses the Commissioner may allow.
(4) The Commissioner may order a legal practitioner suspected of improperly claiming fees to submit a statement and bill of costs for taxation, refunding any excess to the client.
(6) Agreeing to or attempting to collect money contrary to this section is an offence.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Compensation for temporary total or partial disablement
body:
(1) Compensation for temporary total disablement is calculated per Schedule 4, subject to minimum and maximum amounts.
(2) Temporary partial disablement compensation is such portion of that amount as the Commissioner considers equitable.
(3) The employer at the time of the accident is liable for the first three months of this compensation, after which it is repaid to the employer by the Compensation Commissioner or licensee. An employer failing to comply commits an offence.
(4) Payment is by periodical payments, at intervals not exceeding one month.
(5) Periodical payments continue while the temporary total disablement continues, up to 24 months (extendable by the Director-General beyond 12 months).
(6) Temporary total disablement continuing beyond 24 months may be treated as permanent disablement.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Expiry of compensation for temporary total or partial disablement
body:
(1) The right to this compensation expires when the employee is declared medically fit to resume work at the same or greater earnings, or when awarded compensation for permanent disablement.
(2) The Director-General may again award such compensation if the disablement recurs or deteriorates, or the employee needs further medical aid necessitating further absence expected to reduce their disablement.
(3) When re-awarding compensation, the Director-General may suspend any pension payments for the same accident while periodical payments are being received.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Amendment of Schedule 2
body: The Minister may, on the Director-General's recommendation and after consulting the Board, amend Schedule 2 (injuries and disablement percentages) by Gazette notice, following a 60-day public comment period.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Compensation for permanent disablement of employee in training or under 26 years of age
body: If a permanently disabled employee was, at the time of the accident, an apprentice/trainee or under 26 years of age, the Director-General determines their earnings on the more favourable of: for trainees, the earnings of a recently qualified person or someone with 5 years more experience in the same occupation; for those under 26, the earnings a 26-year-old doing the same work would normally receive, or someone with 5 years more experience.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Payment of lump sum in lieu of pension
body:
(1) If a pension doesn't exceed a prescribed amount, the Director-General may pay a lump sum in lieu of it upon the pensioner's application.
(2) If it exceeds that amount, a lump sum may be paid for the portion up to the prescribed amount; if the remaining balance is below the prescribed monthly amount, the whole pension may be commuted.
(3) No pension or portion due to a child may be paid as a lump sum.
(4) The lump sum is calculated as the Director-General determines, subject to control under section 59.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Compensation to employee previously in receipt of compensation
body:
(1) In awarding or reviewing compensation for permanent disablement, the Director-General may take into account any compensation the employee already received under this or any other law for permanent disablement.
(2) If an employee who already received permanent disablement compensation meets with a further accident, the Director-General may calculate compensation for both on the earnings basis most favourable to the employee.
(3) An employee may not be paid pensions in respect of one or more accidents totalling more than the pension for 100 per cent disablement.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Amount of compensation if employee dies
body:
Sets out, in detail, the lump sum and monthly pension payable to a widow/widower and children when an employee dies of an accident, scaled per Schedule 4, with provisions for allocating compensation among multiple dependants, funeral cost payments, and a proviso that total pensions may not exceed what would have been payable for 100 per cent permanent disablement.

Note: this entry summarises a long, detailed section covering multiple dependant scenarios rather than reproducing every subsection verbatim, since the exact figures are set out in Schedule 4 rather than the section text itself.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Amendment of Schedule 4
body: The Minister may, on the Director-General's recommendation and after consulting the Board, amend Schedule 4 (benefit amounts) by Gazette notice, following a 60-day public comment period.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Increase of monthly pensions
body:
(1) The Minister may, after consulting the Commissioner and the Board, increase monthly pensions payable under sections 49 and 54 by Gazette notice, following a 30-day public comment period.
(2) The Minister may differentiate between accidents that happened on different dates.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Advances on compensation
body: In anticipation of a compensation award, the Director-General may advance to or on behalf of an employee such amount as is equitable, given the employee's interests or pressing need, or direct the employer individually liable or licensee to do so.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Control over payment of compensation
body:
(1) Compensation may be paid in instalments or otherwise, invested or applied to the employee's advantage, or paid to the Master of the High Court, a trustee, or another person to apply under determined conditions.
(2) The Director-General may direct that compensation payable by an employer individually liable or licensee instead be paid to the Director-General to be dealt with under subsection (1).
(3) On an employee's or dependant's death, any unpaid compensation balance does not form part of their estate and is paid to a dependant the Director-General designates, or, absent one, to the deceased's estate.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Pensioner resident outside Republic
body:
(1) If a pensioner is resident outside the Republic or absent for more than six months total, the Director-General may award a lump sum in lieu of the pension, ending the right to it.
(2) The Director-General must first notify the pensioner of this intention and invite representations.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Recovery of compensation or other benefits
body:
(1) If an employer individually liable or licensee refuses or fails to pay compensation owed, the Director-General may issue a prescribed order for payment.
(2) A certified copy sent to the relevant magistrate's court clerk has the effect of a civil judgment, with the Director-General having a judgment creditor's powers.
(3) Amounts recovered are paid into the Compensation Fund.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Provisional settlements
body:
(1) The Director-General may authorise an employer individually liable or licensee to provisionally settle employee compensation or medical aid claims, subject to conditions.
(2) Such settlements must be reported to the Director-General, who may confirm, amend, repudiate, or otherwise deal with them.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Manner of calculating earnings
body: Sets out the detailed method for the Director-General to calculate an employee's earnings for compensation purposes, including what to include (food/quarters value, regular overtime) and exclude (intermittent overtime, special expense payments, ex gratia payments), and fallback calculation methods for short-service employees or employees with multiple employers.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Presumption regarding cause of occupational disease
body: If an employee who contracted an occupational disease was employed in work listed in Schedule 3 for that disease, it is presumed (unless the contrary is proved) that the disease arose out of and in the course of their employment.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Notice of occupational disease by employee and employer
body:
(1) An employee must give written notice of a contracted occupational disease to their employer (or last employer) as soon as possible, and may also notify the Commissioner.
(2) The employer must report the disease to the Commissioner or licensee within 14 days of receiving such notice.
(3) An employer who fails to comply commits an offence.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Amendment of Schedule 3
body: The Minister may, on the Director-General's recommendation and after consulting the Board and medical advisory panel chairpersons, amend Schedule 3 (occupational diseases), even retrospectively, following a 60-day public comment period.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Appointment of medical advisory panels
body:
(1) The Director-General may appoint regional medical advisory panels to assist with diagnosing occupational diseases in individual cases, advise on Schedule 3 inclusions, and advise on general diagnosis/disablement policy.
(2)-(4) Panel members are paid prescribed remuneration, one is designated chairman, and appointments may be terminated for misconduct or inability to perform functions.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Director-General to decide on need for, and nature and sufficiency of, medical aid
body: All questions regarding the need for, and the nature and sufficiency of, any medical aid supplied or to be supplied are decided by the Director-General.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Contributions by employees towards cost of medical aid prohibited
body:
(1) An employer who demands or receives a contribution from an employee towards medical aid costs commits an offence.
(2) On conviction, the Director-General may order repayment of the improperly received amount, enforceable the same way as a section 61 order.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Employer to furnish returns of earnings
body:
(1) Employers (excluding certain exempted categories) must furnish the Commissioner with an annual earnings return by 31 March each year.
(1A) An employer commencing business must furnish an estimated-earnings return within 7 days.
(3) If a return understates actual earnings, the Director-General may impose a penalty of up to 10% of the difference.
(5) If an employer fails to furnish a return, or their estimate seems too low, the Director-General may estimate the earnings.
(6) Failure to comply is an offence.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Certain employers exempt from assessment
body:
Sets out categories of employer (including the State, and employers granted individual-liability exemption by the Director-General) exempt from the standard assessment/registration process, instead bearing compensation liability directly themselves.

Note: this entry summarises the section's structure rather than reproducing every category verbatim, since it is a long list of specific exempted categories.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Failure to pay assessment or other moneys
body:
(1) If an employer fails to pay an assessment in accordance with section 86, the Director-General may impose a fine at the prescribed percentage (currently 10 per cent) on the outstanding amount.
(a) If an employer fails to comply with the provisions of section 80(1) (registering with the Compensation Fund) and an employee in his employ meets with an accident, the employer may be held liable for the compensation that would otherwise have been payable from the Compensation Fund.

Note: this entry summarises the section from the confirmed opening subsections rather than reproducing the complete verbatim text of every subsection, since the full text was not fully accessible when this entry was written.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Review of decisions by Director-General
body:
(1) The Director-General may, after notice (if possible) to the party concerned and after giving that party an opportunity to submit representations, at any time review any decision made in connection with a claim for compensation or the award of compensation, on the ground that-
(a) the employee has not submitted himself to an examination referred to in section 42;
and other similar grounds relating to new or previously unavailable information.

Note: this entry summarises the section from the confirmed opening subsection rather than reproducing the complete verbatim text. The Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Amendment Act 10 of 2022 further empowers the Commissioner to review pension claims or awards under this section at any time, specifically for the purpose of re-assessing permanent disablement - a new power that did not exist before the 2022 amendment.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Contributions by employers individually liable and mutual associations
body:
(1) Notwithstanding any provision to the contrary contained in this Act, employers individually liable and mutual associations shall pay annually to the Director-General, in such manner and at such times as he may determine, such portion of the expenditure incurred by him in the administration of the provisions of this Act as he may deem equitable.
(2) The Director-General shall, as soon as possible after the end of each financial year, estimate the loss suffered during that year as a result of compensation that became payable out of the Compensation Fund in respect of employees whose employers failed to pay assessments as required.

Note: this entry summarises the section from the confirmed opening subsections rather than reproducing the complete verbatim text of every subsection, since the full text was not fully accessible when this entry was written.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Objections and appeal against decisions of Director-General
body:
(1) Any person aggrieved by a decision of the Director-General may lodge an objection with the Director-General within 90 days of receiving notice of that decision.

Note: this entry summarises the section from confirmed secondary sources rather than reproducing the complete verbatim text of every subsection, since the full text was not fully accessible when this entry was written. The 90-day objection period is confirmed via multiple independent occupational health training sources.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Director-General may state case for Supreme Court
body:
If neither of the assessors agrees with the view of the presiding officer on a matter, the presiding officer shall submit the dispute to the Supreme Court (now the High Court) for decision.
Any person affected by such a decision may appeal to any provincial or local division of the High Court having jurisdiction, in respect of decisions regarding whether an accident or occupational disease causing disablement or death was attributable to the employee's serious and wilful misconduct, whether the amount of compensation awarded is so excessive or inadequate that it could not reasonably have been made, or the right to increased compensation under section 56.
The presiding officer may make an order as to costs in connection with proceedings under this section.

Note: this entry summarises the section from confirmed secondary sources rather than reproducing the complete verbatim text of every subsection.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Arrangements with foreign states regarding compensation
body:
The Republic may enter into arrangements with other states-
(a) to determine, in any case where an employee is entitled to compensation both in terms of this Act and in terms of the law of any such state, under the law of which state such employee or his dependants shall be entitled to recover compensation;
(b) to authorise the Director-General to allow evidence taken in any such state, and to obtain and take evidence for use in such state or for the facilitation of proceedings for the recovery of compensation in terms of the law of any such state.

Note: this entry summarises the section from confirmed secondary sources rather than reproducing the complete verbatim text of every subsection.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Failure to comply with this Act
body:
(1) Any person, including an employer, who contravenes, or fails to comply with, any-
(a) provision of this Act;
(b) regulation; or
(c) condition, suspension, notice, order, instruction, prohibition, authorisation, permission, consent, exemption, certificate or document determined, given, issued, prescribed or granted by or under this Act by the Minister, Chief Inspector of Mines, inspector, any person authorised under section 49(4) or any person to whom any power has been delegated or the performance of any duty has been assigned under section 96,
commits an offence and is liable to a fine or imprisonment as may be prescribed.
(1B) Any employer is liable to a fine in terms of section 55B if the employer contravenes, or fails to comply with, any-
(a) provision of this Act;
(b) regulation; or
(c) condition, suspension, notice, order, instruction, prohibition, authorisation, permission, consent, exemption, certificate or document determined, given, issued, promulgated or granted by or under this Act by the Minister, Chief Inspector of Mines, inspector, any person authorised under section 49(4) or any person to whom any power has been delegated or the performance of any duty has been assigned under section 96.
(1C) Despite subsection (1B), an employer who contravenes or fails to comply with any standard in a code of practice prepared in terms of section 9(2) is not liable to a fine in terms of section 55B in certain circumstances set out in the rest of this subsection.

Note: this section is now complete through subsection (1C)'s opening words - the remainder of subsection (1C) and any further subsections were not accessible at the point the source document was fetched.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Penalties
body:
(1) Any person convicted of an offence in terms of section 87, may be sentenced to a fine or to imprisonment to be determined by the court.
(2) Any person convicted of an offence in terms of section 90(a) or (b)(i), may be sentenced to the penalty applicable to a similar offence in a magistrate's court.
(3) Any person convicted of an offence in terms of section 90(c)(ii), may be sentenced to any penalty that may be imposed in law for perjury.
(4) Any person convicted of an offence in terms of this Act for which no penalty is otherwise expressly determined, may be sentenced to a fine or to imprisonment for a period not exceeding six months.
(5) Any person convicted of an offence in terms of any section mentioned in Column 1 of Table 1 of Schedule 8, may be sentenced to a fine or to imprisonment for a period not exceeding the period mentioned in Column 2 of that Table opposite the number of that section.
(6) Any owner convicted of an offence in terms of section 86 or 86A may be sentenced to withdrawal or suspension of the permit, or a fine of three million rands or a period of imprisonment not exceeding five years or to both such fine or imprisonment.
(7) In the event of a conviction, the court may, in addition to imposing a sentence, order the person convicted to repair any damage caused, to the satisfaction of the Chief Inspector of Mines, and comply with a provision of this Act within a specified period of time.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Serving of documents
body:
Unless otherwise provided in this Act, a notice, order or other document which, in terms of this Act, must be served on or delivered to a person, will have been properly served or delivered if it has been either-
(a) served on or delivered to that person; or
(b) sent by registered post to that person's last known address; or
(c) published in the Gazette.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Proof of facts
body:
In any legal proceedings in terms of this Act-
(a) if it is alleged that a person at a mine is or was an employee, that person is presumed to be an employee at that mine, unless the contrary is proved;
(b) if it is proved that a false statement, entry or information appears in or on a book, plan, record or other document, the person who kept that document is presumed to have made, entered, recorded or stored that statement, entry, record or information, unless the contrary is proved; and
(c) subject to the provisions of sections 63(1), 63(3) and 71(2), any statement, entry or information in or on any book, plan, record or other document is admissible in evidence as an admission of the facts in or on it by the person who made, entered, recorded or stored it unless it is proved that that person did not make, enter, record or store it within the scope of their functions.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Delegation and exercise of power
body:
(1) The Minister may delegate any power conferred upon the Minister by or under this Act, except the power to make regulations, to the Chief Inspector of Mines.
(2) The Chief Inspector of Mines may delegate any power or assign any performance of any duty conferred or imposed upon the Chief Inspector of Mines by or under this Act, or any other law, to any inspector, any other person with appropriate knowledge and experience who is under the control of the Chief Inspector of Mines, or any other person, after consulting the Council.
(3) A delegation or assignment must be in writing, and may be subject to any conditions or restrictions determined by the Minister or Chief Inspector of Mines, as the case may be.
(4) A delegation does not prevent the exercise of that power by the Minister or Chief Inspector of Mines, as the case may be.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Minister's power to add and change Schedules
body:
(1) The Minister, after consulting the Council, by notice in the Gazette may add to, change or replace any Schedule to this Act other than Schedules 2, 3 and 7 and, subject to subsection (5), Schedule 4.
(2) The Minister, after consulting the Council, by notice in the Gazette may add to this Act a further Schedule containing matters in respect of which health and safety committees may consult.
(3) The Minister, after consulting the Council, by notice in the Gazette, may add to this Act a further Schedule containing the constitution of the Council and its committees.
(4) The Minister, after consulting the Council and the Mining Qualifications Authority, by notice in the Gazette may add to this Act a further Schedule containing the constitution of the Mining Qualifications Authority and its committees.
(5) The Minister, after consulting the Council, by notice in the Gazette may add to Schedule 4 further items containing transitional provisions necessary for the implementation of this Act.
(6) The Minister, after consulting the Council and in consultation with the Minister of Health, by notice in the Gazette may add to this Act a further Schedule to suspend or vary the application of the Occupational Diseases in Mines and Works Act, 1973 (Act 78 of 1973), except in relation to the determination or payment of compensation.
(7) The Minister may add to, change or replace any page header or sidenote by notice in the Gazette.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Regulations
body:
(1) The Minister, after consulting the Council, by notice in the Gazette may make regulations regarding a very wide range of matters, including: health and safety of persons at mines; health and safety standards, codes of practice, protective clothing and equipment; work by employees exposed to a health hazard; health and safety management systems; orderly operations at mines; duties of employees and employers; permits and accreditation for machinery/equipment; conditions for erecting or using machinery; elimination and control of hazards; safe handling, storage, transport and disposal of hazardous substances and explosives; protection of equipment, structures, water sources and land surfaces; making safe of undermined ground, excavations, tailings and waste dumps; monitoring environmental aspects affecting health and safety; housing and nutrition standards; fitness-to-work standards; occupational hygiene measurement and medical surveillance standards; accident/disease reporting and record-keeping; exit certificates; application and document forms; mine plans and statistical reports; health and safety representative and committee matters (qualifications, elections, terms of office, functions, training); Council and Mining Qualifications Authority appointments and funding; inspector qualifications; research funding accounts; inquiry procedures; appeal procedures; fees; health and safety levies; obligations relating to safe-making of dangerous conditions; plain language requirements; the fine system under sections 55A/55B; and minimum standards for mine rescue services.
(2) No regulation may be made relating to State revenue or expenditure except with the concurrence of the Minister of Finance, or any health matter, except after consultation with the Minister for Health.
(3) The Minister, after consultation with the Mining Qualifications Authority, by notice in the Gazette, may make regulations on qualifications, examinations, certificates of competency, funding, assessor accreditation, examination bodies, quality assurance, and related Mining Qualifications Authority matters.
(4) Regulations made in terms of subsection (3) must be in accordance with the National Qualifications Framework approved in terms of the South African Qualifications Authority Act, 1995.
(5) The Minister may incorporate all or part of any health and safety standard, without restating the text of it, in a regulation by referring to the number, title and year of issue of that standard.
(6) The Minister must consult the Council before incorporating a health and safety standard in a regulation.
(7) The Minister, after consulting the Council, by notice in the Gazette, may make regulations imposing any function of an employer on any person, other than the employer, who employs employees.
(8)-(12) Deal with the technical status of incorporated health and safety standards, keeping a register of them, public inspection of that register, and confirming that section 31 of the Standards Act, 1993 does not apply to such incorporations.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Amendment of laws
body: Each of the laws referred to in Schedule 3 is hereby amended to the extent specified in that Schedule.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Transitional arrangements
body:
(1) The amendment of laws referred to in Schedule 3 does not affect any transitional arrangement made in Schedule 4.
(2) The transitional arrangements in Schedule 4 must be read and applied as substantive provisions of this Act.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Interpretation
body:
(2) Subject to sections 26 and 33, no agreement may affect any provision of this Act, any condition, notice, order, instruction, prohibition, authorisation, permission, consent, exemption, certificate or document determined, given, issued, promulgated or granted by or under this Act by the Minister, Chief Inspector of Mines, inspector or any other person authorised under this Act, or any condition contained in any exemption.
(3) Subsection (2) applies to any agreement whether entered into before or after the commencement of this Act or before or after the issuing of the documents referred to in subsection (2).
(4) Any notice, order or any other document issued in good faith in terms of this Act, is valid according to its terms, despite any want of form or lack of power on the part of any person to issue or authenticate it, provided the necessary power is subsequently conferred upon that person.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Definitions

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Occupational Health and Safety Act, 1993, not applicable
body: The Occupational Health and Safety Act, 1993 (Act 85 of 1993), is not applicable to any matter in respect of which any provision of this Act is applicable.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Civil liability of State
body: The State Liability Act, 1957 (Act 20 of 1957), applies with the changes required by the context in respect of the Mine Health and Safety Inspectorate, and in such application a reference in that Act to the Minister of a department concerned must be construed as a reference to the Chief Inspector of Mines.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Act binds State
body: The provisions of this Act bind the State except in so far as any criminal liability is concerned.

collection: Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996
title: Short title and commencement
body:
(1) This Act is called the Mine Health and Safety Act, 1996.
(2) This Act comes into operation on a date fixed by the President by Proclamation in the Government Gazette.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Evidence
body:
(1) The record of any decision or award made by the Director-General, and a copy of or extract from a record or document kept by the Director-General or lodged with him, which purports to be certified by the Director-General as a true copy or extract shall upon its mere production in a court of law be prima facie evidence of the content of such record or document.
(2) In any proceedings in terms of this Act, or in any court of law, any document purporting to be a sworn statement made by the Director-General or an authorised person, stating that any person is an employer, mandator, contractor, employee or dependant; that any person was required to pay an amount; that an amount has or has not been paid on a specified date; or that a power under this Act was exercised, shall upon its mere production be prima facie evidence of the facts stated therein.
(3) The person presiding at the court or other proceedings may cause the person who made a sworn statement to be subpoenaed to give viva voce evidence or cause written interrogatories to be sent to them for answering, and a document purporting to be a sworn statement with the answers shall upon its mere production be prima facie evidence of the facts stated therein.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Certain documents exempt from stamp duty
body: Notwithstanding any provision to the contrary contained in any other law, any sworn statement, certificate, receipt or other document required or issued under this Act, shall be exempt from stamp duty.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Disclosure of information
body:
(1) No person shall disclose any information obtained by him in the performance of his functions in terms of this Act, except to the extent necessary for the proper administration of a provision of this Act, for the purposes of the administration of justice, or at the request of the Minister or any other person entitled thereto.
(2) Any person who contravenes the provisions of subsection (1) shall be guilty of an offence.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Regulations
body:
(1) The Minister may make regulations, after consultation with the Board, regarding the place and procedure of meetings and proceedings under this Act; fees payable to medical practitioners or chiropractors; the procedure for paying assessments and fines to the Director-General; the persons, places and manner of payment of assessments; the amount and manner of payment of benefits to assessors; the disposal of unclaimed moneys; and any other matter necessary or expedient to further the objects and purposes of this Act. Following the 2022 amendment, this also includes the rehabilitation, reintegration and return to work; the inspection, compliance and enforcement of this Act; the determination and calculation of permanent disablement; and the appointment of assessors, presiding officers and interpreters.
(2) Different regulations may be made in respect of different classes of employers and employees and of different areas.
(3) Any person who contravenes or fails to comply with any regulation made under subsection (1) shall be guilty of an offence and liable on conviction to a fine, or imprisonment for a period not exceeding six months.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: False statements
body: Any person who in connection with a claim for compensation in terms of this Act, or in any return, notice, report or statement to be given, made or furnished in terms of this Act, makes or causes to be made any statement which is false in a material respect, knowing it to be false, shall be guilty of an offence.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Penalties
body:
Any person who does not comply with the provisions of sections 39, 40, 47, 64, 68, 81, 82 and 83 of this Act shall be liable to a penalty or penalties as specified in the said sections.

This reflects the current text as substituted by the Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Amendment Act 10 of 2022, replacing the previous general penalty (a fine or imprisonment of up to one year for any offence under the Act) with penalties tied to the specific sections listed.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Repeal of laws
body:
(1) Subject to the provisions of this section, the laws specified in Schedule 1 (the Workmen's Compensation Act, 1941 and its various amendment Acts, and section 2 of the Second Black Laws Amendment Act, 1970) are hereby repealed to the extent set out in that Schedule.
(2) Any regulation made, any direction, order or directive issued, any request made or any requirement prescribed and any other thing done under a provision of the Workmen's Compensation Act, and which could be made, issued, prescribed or done under a provision of this Act, shall be deemed to have been made, issued, prescribed or done under the corresponding provision of this Act.
(3) Any claim for compensation or medical aid under a law repealed by subsection (1) in respect of an accident that happened, or a scheduled disease contracted, prior to the commencement of this Act shall be dealt with in terms of the repealed law as if this Act had not been passed, and any right or privilege acquired or accrued under the repealed law is not affected by the repeal.

collection: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993
title: Short title
body:
(1) This Act shall be called the Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act, 1993, and shall come into operation on a date fixed by the State President by proclamation in the Gazette.
(2) Different dates may be fixed under subsection (1) in respect of different provisions of this Act.

title: Jurisdiction
body:
(1) Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in any other law, a magistrate's court shall have jurisdiction to impose any penalty prescribed by this Act or any specific Environmental Management Acts.
(2) Where a competent authority is of the view that a more severe penalty could be considered than those penalties referred to in section 49B, the competent authority may request the National Prosecuting Authority to institute the criminal proceedings in the High Court.

title: Prohibition of certain products
body: The Minister may from time to time regulate, prohibit or control the production, sale, distribution, import or export of products that may have a substantial detrimental effect on the environment.

title: Delegation of powers and duties by Minister responsible for water affairs
body:
(1) The Minister responsible for water affairs may delegate a power or duty vested in him or her in terms of this Act to an official in the department responsible for water affairs.
(2) A delegation in terms of subsection (1) must be in writing, may be subject to conditions, does not prevent the exercise of the power or the performance of the duty by the Minister responsible for water affairs personally, may include the power to subdelegate, may be withdrawn by the Minister responsible for water affairs subject to any rights that may have accrued to any person, and does not divest the Minister responsible for water affairs of the responsibility for the exercise of the power or the performance of the duty.

title: Delegation of powers and duties by municipal manager
body:
(1) The municipal manager of a municipality may delegate a power or duty vested in him or her in terms of this Act to an official in the municipality.
(2) A delegation in terms of subsection (1) must be in writing, may be subject to conditions, does not prevent the exercise of the power or the performance of the duty by the municipal manager personally, and may be withdrawn by the municipal manager subject to any rights that may have accrued to any person.

title: Extension of time periods applicable to appeals relating to prospecting, exploration, mining or production
body: The Minister responsible for mineral resources in respect of a decision that relates to prospecting, exploration, mining or production in terms of this Act or any specific environmental management Act may only in exceptional circumstances extend or condone a failure by a person to comply with a time period in terms of this Act or a specific environmental management Act, except a time period which binds the Minister responsible for mineral resources.

title: Condonation of time periods applicable to appeals relating to prospecting, exploration, mining or production
body:
(1) The Minister may only in exceptional circumstances extend or condone a failure by a person to comply with a time period applicable to an appeal contemplated in section 43(1A), except for a time period which binds the Minister.
(2) The Minister may not accept an application for condonation to submit such an appeal after 30 days has lapsed from the date of the decision by the Minister responsible for mineral resources or any person acting under his or her delegated authority.
(3) When considering an extension or condonation the Minister must consider the degree of lateness, a detailed explanation of the reasons for the lateness, whether and to what extent the person or the Minister responsible for mineral resources will suffer prejudice if the time period is extended or condoned, and a detailed explanation of the merits of the application.
(4) The time period may only be condoned for a maximum period equal to the time period allowed for the action for which condonation is sought.
